label: FP
reason: Both alerts are False Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss): The sink is ESAPI.encoder().encodeForHTML(results.toString()). Although CodeQL traces taint from param to bar to sql to results, the variable bar is reassigned in doSomething to map11607.get("keyA-11607") ("a_Value") before sql is constructed, making results independent of user input. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection): The sink is the sql string construction. Due to the same reassignment (bar = map11607.get("keyA-11607")), the final value of bar used in sql is the constant "a_Value", not the user-provided param. Neither sink contains attacker-controlled data.

evidence.note: In doSomething, param is put into map11607, then bar is reassigned to map11607.get("keyA-11607") ("a_Value"). This prevents user input from reaching the final bar value used in sql.
sql is constructed using bar, which resolves to the safe constant "a_Value" due to the reassignment in doSomething.
XSS sink prints results derived from the safe sql query, confirming no user input reaches the HTML output.
